artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled on a matter involving Metropolitan New York Presbytery's handling of a session that permitted a woman to expound Scripture during worship and held services without sermons. The SJC remitted the matter to the Presbytery to complete its work and report to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, while critiquing the procedural manner in which the matter was referred to the SJC.

artifacts.title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present). The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that Anna Lewis's BCO 40-5 report filed directly with the SJC was out of order, holding that the SJC's only responsibility under Chapter 40 arises upon referral from the General Assembly per RAO 16-10.c. Six members dissented, arguing the SJC has historically exercised direct jurisdiction over BCO 40-5 reports and that the majority's interpretation was overly narrow and a departure from settled precedent.

artifacts.title: Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Dailey complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in upholding its Moderator's ruling that a church member's document was administratively in order as a complaint under BCO 43-3, after the Session had ruled it out of order. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that neither triggering condition of BCO 43-3 was met because the Session's ruling that the document did not qualify as a BCO 43-1 complaint was not equivalent to denying it, and the Session had considered and responded to the matter in a timely manner. A substantial dissent argued for a broader interpretation of 'fails to consider' in BCO 43-3.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reported that South Florida Presbytery responded to the citation issued by the 43rd General Assembly. The SJC found most responses satisfactory, but found one response unsatisfactory (regarding charges against a TE that were not properly processed under BCO 32-2), and noted an additional exception of substance regarding improper divestiture under BCO 46-8.

artifacts.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Mitchell appealed his indefinite suspension from office as Ruling Elder by the Presbytery of the Ascension, arising from allegations he broke a promise to take a sabbatical from Session and failed in his duties as Clerk of Session. The SJC vacated the judgment on Specification No. 2 (promise-breaking) and remanded for possible new trial, and reversed and dismissed Specification No. 6 (clerk duties) as insufficiently serious to warrant trial.

artifacts.title: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

artifacts.title: Brown v. Northern California Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.title: PCA v. Gulfstream
artifacts.synopsis: Gulfstream Presbytery was cited and appeared before the SJC regarding exceptions of substance found in its records; the SJC accepted the presbytery's response as acceptable, pending certification that the response was approved by the presbytery.
